ticker: Trump, Xi, and Putin hold historic trilateral talks in China.
Cyclone Akvan approaches Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coasts with heavy rain.
India to charge bulk Scotch imports 162.5% duty and tax.
Gold drops to a 14-month low amid hawkish Federal Reserve rhetoric.
Microsoft CEO warns that AI replacing human workers threatens democracy.

articles.headline: India Imposes 162.5% Duty on Bulk Scotch Imports
articles.brief: India is set to impose a heavy 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch whisky imports amid an ongoing standoff with the United Kingdom regarding trade pact negotiations.

articles.headline: Gold Plunges to 14-Month Low on Hawkish Fed Rhetoric
articles.brief: Gold prices fell sharply to a 14-month low as the strengthening U.S. dollar and rising Treasury yields weighed heavily on the precious metal following hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve officials.

articles.headline: Severe Cyclone Akvan Forces Mass Evacuations in India
articles.brief: Nearly 50,000 residents have been evacuated as Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan tracks northward over the Bay of Bengal, threatening a direct landfall between Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts.

articles.headline: Trump, Xi, and Putin Meet in Historic Trilateral Summit
articles.brief: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin convened for landmark trilateral discussions on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China, addressing global security and trade.

articles.headline: Microsoft CEO Warns AI Replacing Labor Threatens Democracy
articles.brief: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella cautioned that widespread displacement of human workers by artificial intelligence could destabilize democratic institutions, emphasizing the critical balance required between capital and labor.

articles.headline: Governments Issue Urgent Warnings Over Critical Java Flaw
articles.brief: Global cybersecurity authorities have issued severe warnings regarding a newly uncovered vulnerability in Java that leaves numerous computer systems and enterprise networks vulnerable to malicious attacks.

articles.headline: India Proposes Legal Quality Mandates for Blood Centres
articles.brief: In an effort to tighten medical safety standards, the Indian government is planning to make external quality check participation legally binding under the Drugs Rules for all registered blood centres.

articles.headline: Sunil Questions Omission of Mohammed Siraj from Playing XI
articles.brief: Cricket legend Sunil Gavaskar has publicly questioned the team management's decision to omit pacer Mohammed Siraj, noting his strong track record and consistent performances for the national side.
